start.dev.pi.d: A Pi 4 or 5 with a touch screen makes a tidy, low-cost till.
start.dev.pc.d: Any 64-bit Windows or Linux machine works — give it a second life.
start.dev.mac.d: Apple Silicon Macs (M1 and newer) run it natively.

faq.title: Questions shop owners ask
faq.sub: EPOS, POS, till system or cash register — what Universal Till is, and what it costs.
faq.q1: Is Universal Till an EPOS system?
faq.a1: Yes. EPOS (electronic point of sale), POS, till system and cash register all mean the software you ring up sales on. Universal Till gives you a touch sale screen, barcode scanning, receipts, stock and sales reports.
faq.a2: Yes. The till itself is free forever on your own hardware: open source under the MIT licence, no monthly fee for the core. Paid plans have no minimum term on monthly billing; in Germany, the managed TSE line (optional, from Shop) has a 12-month minimum per activated main till. Optional cloud extras, such as off-site backup, may cost extra, and card payments carry your card provider's own fees.
faq.a3: Yes. A full sale completes with no internet at all, and everything works locally on the till. Syncing is a bonus, never a requirement. A card reader still needs whatever connection its own provider requires.
faq.a4: A Raspberry Pi, an old PC or laptop, a mini-PC or a proper touch terminal — there are downloads for Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi and Android. The iPhone and iPad apps are in internal testing (not on the App Store yet). A complete DIY till costs from about £70.
faq.a5: Yes. We never sit in your money flow: use any card machine and any processor — no fee creep, no frozen payouts.
faq.q6: Can I move from my current till?
faq.a6: Yes. Export your catalogue from your current system and import it: Loyverse, Square, SumUp and Shopify exports are recognised automatically, and any CSV or Excel file with name and price columns works. You see a preview before anything is saved.

dl.title: Download Universal Till
dl.sub: Free and offline-first. Pick your device — we've guessed the best one for you.
dl.lxarm.d: ARM boards other than Raspberry Pi.
dl.android.d: Android 7.0+. Sideloaded — not on the Play Store.
dl.android.note: Android's installer will warn about "unknown sources" the first time — that's expected for an app outside the Play Store, not a sign anything is wrong. Tap through to allow it.
dl.next: Windows installer, macOS app, Raspberry Pi/Linux .deb: the till opens in its own app window — no browser, no terminal. Windows: run the installer, then launch "Universal Till" from the Start menu/desktop shortcut. macOS: open the .dmg, drag Universal Till into Applications and open it — the app is Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS only asks you once to confirm. Raspberry Pi/Debian/Ubuntu .deb: after sudo apt install ./unitill-pos_*.deb, "Universal Till" is in your applications menu. Portable .tar.gz/.zip archives: on Windows and Linux, double-click unitill-desktop.exe / unitill-desktop for the same app-window experience; run-unitill.command/.sh/.bat opens your default browser instead. The macOS portable archive is not notarized: the first time, macOS blocks run-unitill.command — open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. Dedicated Raspberry Pi till (no desktop needed): on a fresh Raspberry Pi OS Lite install, reboot once after installing the .deb — the first boot sets up the kiosk, and from then on the Pi starts straight into the till, fullscreen, no desktop at all. On Raspberry Pi OS with Desktop, the till opens fullscreen on top of the desktop when you log in; Settings → Display → "Exit to OS window" (manager PIN) takes you back to the desktop.

meta.android-till.desc: Turn an Android tablet into a till. Universal Till is a free, open-source EPOS app for Android 7.0 and newer that keeps selling with no internet.
android.title: Android till app: free EPOS for Android tablets
android.lede: Turn an Android tablet into a full till. The whole till runs on the tablet itself, so a sale completes with no internet at all. Free and open source, with no monthly fee for the core.
android.note: Android 7.0 or newer · installed from our website, not Google Play yet
android.shot: The sale screen, the same on an Android tablet as on every other till
android.what.title: What you get on an Android tablet
android.what.same.t: The same till, not a cut-down app
android.what.same.d: The Android app runs the very same till as the Windows, Mac and Raspberry Pi versions: the sale screen, catalogue, stock, receipts and reports.
android.what.offline.d: Everything is stored on the tablet. If the Wi-Fi drops, the status bar says so and you keep ringing up sales.
android.what.bt.d: Pair a Bluetooth barcode scanner or scale from inside the till. Android asks you once to allow Bluetooth.
android.what.multi.d: An Android tablet can be your main till or join another till on your shop's network, and sales sync between them.
android.what.kiosk.d: Set a tablet to self-order and customers order on it themselves. The till asks Android to pin the screen, which blocks Home and Recents while it stays pinned.
android.what.update.d: When a new version is out, tap the update chip, then confirm in Android's own installer. The first time, Android also asks you to allow the install.
android.setup.title: Set up an Android till
android.setup.s1: On the tablet, open the download page and tap the Android app. Most tablets need the 64-bit version; the page picks it for you.
android.setup.s2: When Android asks, allow installing from unknown sources. Play Protect may say it hasn't seen the app before: tap Scan app, then install.
android.setup.s3: Open Universal Till and follow the setup: your language, your shop's country and its name. Then add your products.
android.limits.i1: The app isn't on Google Play yet. You download it from this website.
android.limits.i2: Android doesn't let an app replace itself silently, so every update needs one tap in Android's installer.
android.limits.i3: An Android till that joins a main till doesn't update itself to match: install the new version on it by hand.
android.limits.i4: Card payments go through your own card machine and provider, which may need its own connection.
android.limits.i5: Screen pinning is Android's standard pin: it only starts once you accept Android's prompt, and someone who knows Android's unpin gesture can still leave it. For a lock that can't be undone, the tablet must be set up as a managed device.
android.faq.title: Android till questions
android.faq.q1: Does the tablet need Wi-Fi or mobile data?
android.faq.a1: Not to sell: a sale completes on the tablet with no connection at all. Wi-Fi is needed to work with other tills on your shop's network and to download updates, and a card machine needs whatever connection its own provider requires.
android.faq.q2: Can an Android tablet work alongside a Windows or Raspberry Pi till?
android.faq.a2: Yes. Every version runs the same till, so one shop can mix them: the Android tablet can be the main till, or join a main till on another platform over your shop's network.
android.faq.a3: Not yet. Download the app from our download page. Android warns you the first time because the app comes from outside Google Play; that is expected.
android.faq.q4: Which tablets does it run on?
android.faq.a4: Android 7.0 or newer. There is a 64-bit version for most tablets, one for older 32-bit tablets, and a universal one if you're not sure.
